Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the UniBank Financial Group Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, the instructions are to press star one to ask a question. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review UniBank Financial Group's results for the third quarter. With me this morning are Alex Harper, Chief Executive Officer; Jennifer Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Mark Rodriguez, Chief Risk Officer; Karen Wong, Chief Credit Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Laura Chen, Chief Operating Officer; David Kim, Chief Marketing Officer; and Susan Bailey, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Alex Harper.

Alex Harper:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. UniBank Financial Group delivered record results in the third quarter, exceeding all previous benchmarks and solidifying our position as a leader in the financial services industry.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on sustaining strong revenue growth, driving operational efficiency, managing risk effectively, investing in technology and innovation, enhancing customer experience, strengthening our brand reputation, promoting a diverse and inclusive culture, and delivering superior returns to our shareholders.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on key areas of performance. First, our efficiency ratio saw substantial progress, reaching 58.2% with clear paths to mid-50s targets through digital transformation and cost discipline. Revenue diversification has reshaped our mix, with non-interest income now over half of total revenue, reducing volatility significantly. Overall, we posted record adjusted net revenues of $8.7 billion, up 12% year-over-year, with strong net interest income and diversified fee growth. Market conditions boosted non-interest income, particularly in investment banking and wealth management amid equity rallies. Deposits grew robustly to $520 billion, with strategic shifts in mix toward higher-yield savings while preserving core low-cost transactional balances. We released reserves reflecting improving credit metrics and macroeconomic stability, maintaining peer-leading coverage ratios. Risk-weighted assets declined through proactive management, bolstering our CET1 to 13.2%. Finally, we outlook modest loan growth of 4-6% with pristine credit quality into next year.

I will now turn the call over to Jennifer Lee to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jennifer Lee:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning. UniBank Financial Group reported net income of $2.4 billion for the third quarter, or $2.18 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 9% year-over-year, driven by growth in our loan portfolio and improved net interest margin. Non-interest income was up 15% year-over-year, reflecting strong performance in our investment banking and wealth management businesses. We are generating strong returns on equity and are committed to delivering value to our shareholders.

Let me expand on these results with more specifics, starting with our overall company performance highlights, which reflect resilient execution amid elevated rates, easing inflation, and geopolitical challenges. For the quarter ended September 30, 2024, we reported record adjusted net revenues of $8.7 billion, up 12% year-over-year and 4% quarter-over-quarter. This marks our eighth straight quarter of double-digit revenue growth, powered by asset-sensitive positioning and balance sheet discipline. Adjusted net income hit $2.4 billion, up 15% year-over-year, with diluted EPS of $2.18, surpassing consensus by 6%. ROTCE expanded to 18.2%, above our 17% target, while ROA was 1.45% and efficiency ratio improved to 52.3%.

Net interest income, our core engine, grew 14% to $6.2 billion, with NIM up 21 basis points quarter-over-quarter to 3.65%, thanks to higher loan yields at 5.8% outpacing deposit costs at 2.1%, supported by 65% low-cost or non-interest-bearing deposits. Average loans rose 9% to $450 billion, balanced across C&I up 11% to $180 billion, residential mortgages steady at $120 billion, and consumer up 8% to $90 billion. Non-interest income of $2.5 billion rose 7%, led by wealth fees up 20% to $850 million on record $1.2 trillion AUM, card fees up 12%, and MSR hedging gains.

Deposits hit $520 billion, up 7%, with loan-to-deposit at 86%. Liquidity metrics are strong: LCR 125%, NSFR 118%. Capital is robust with CET1 at 11.8%, enabling $1.2 billion share repurchases and a 10% dividend hike to $0.62. Credit quality shines with criticized loans at 1.8%, NCOs at 22 bps, NPLs 0.65%, ACL 1.45% or 220% of NPLs, and a $100 million reserve release. Our $40 billion CRE book is 70% multifamily/industrial.

Regionally, U.S. (70% revenue) gained market share in Southeast/Midwest; Europe flat but ESG lending up; Asia-Pacific up 30%. Tech investments like PinnacleOne platform with 15 million users, GenAI fraud detection, and blockchain pilots drove efficiency.

Turning now to our efficiency ratio, a cornerstone of profitability at UniBank. It's adjusted non-interest expenses over total revenue. In Q3, we achieved 58.2%, a 410 basis point year-over-year improvement from 62.3% and 110 basis points sequential from 59.3%—our best since 2019 pre-pandemic, at the strong end of peers versus KBW median 61% and JPMorgan's 56%.

Drivers include expense growth of just 2.1% to $4.2 billion versus 7.8% revenue to $7.2 billion, NIM up 12 bps to 3.45% from C&I loans and securities shifts. Digital transformation automated 45% of workflows via RPA with UiPath/Blue Prism on Temenos, saving $150 million annualized and cutting consumer costs 28%. Cloud to AWS/Azure 65% complete, TCO down 22%, adding 80 bps to efficiency. Branch optimization closed 120 sites, pivoted to fintech partnerships like Plaid/Stripe, generating $85 million gains and digital transactions to 72%.

U.S. (72% revenue) at 55.8% efficiency from mortgage refis and Zelle share; Europe (18%) to 62.4% via SWIFT GPI; Asia-Pacific (10%) at 59.1% from wealth fees amid China reopening. Our Efficiency 2.0 rationalized 15% low-margin products, redeployed to ESG lending with BlackRock.

We're raising FY24 guidance to 57-58%, targeting mid-50s (54-55%) by FY26 via $300 million GenAI savings with Palantir, 20% headcount optimization, and PayForge acquisition. Risks like FDIC costs noted, but CET1 11.8% provides buffer. This drove ROE to 13.2%.

Next, our revenue diversification initiatives, rebalancing from NII-dominant peers. Q3 total revenue $14.2 billion, up 8%, non-interest now 58% versus 42% three years ago and industry 48%. Revenue volatility down 22%. Wealth AUM $620 billion, up 18%, inflows $12.4 billion, fees $1.8 billion up 22% on ESG ETFs. Payments via UniPay $1.1 trillion volume, fees $1.2 billion up 24%, API marketplace 4,500 fintechs. Investment banking $2.1 billion up 16%, #8 in leagues. Insurance premiums $900 million up 14%, combined ratio 92%.

Regions: North America non-NII +15%; EMEA +12%; APAC/LatAm +22%. Diversification stabilized NIM at 3.45%, buffered deposit betas. Targeting $2 billion incremental non-NII by 2025 via robo-advisory, fintech JVs, ESG tokens. Non-NII CAGR 20% versus NII peers 5%, raised FY24 guidance 56-58%.

On the impact of market conditions on non-interest income, which hit $2.8 billion up 14% year-over-year and 8% quarter-over-quarter—28% of revenue mix. Investment banking $850 million up 22% on M&A/ECM amid S&P gains, HY spreads tightening. Markets $650 million up 9%, equities +25% on VIX 19, FX +12%; fixed income dipped. Wealth $720 million up 16% on $1.7 trillion AUM. Cards/payments $450 million up 11%. Deposit charges down 4% on waivers.

Tech like RevAI boosts internalization; robo-advisory $150 billion AUM. Q4 guide $2.9-3.1 billion assuming S&P flat/up 5%.

Deposit growth totaled $238.4 billion up 8.7% year-over-year, outpacing industry. Transactional 42% mix ($100.1 billion) up 3.8%, pressured by betas to 65%. Savings 38% ($90.6 billion) up 12.4%, beta 82%. Time 20% ($47.7 billion) up 22.1%, rates 4.65%. Trends: yield chase post-SVB, digital shifts up 28%.

Strategies: AI optimizers, relationship rewards, regional tailoring (Southeast branches, Midwest acquisition), cap brokered at 5%. Guide 5-7% FY growth, core 43-45%.

On reserves, we released $450 million PCL, YTD $1.1 billion versus prior build, per CECL with macro reversion—unemployment 4.2%, home prices +3.2%. NCOs 2.45%, delinqs 3.9%. Consumer release $600 million, C&I flat, RE build $50 million. U.S. strong, Europe/Asia mixed. ACL 1.52% ($12.4 billion), 285% NPLs—peer leading.

Tech upgrades cut forecast error 18%. Expect neutral Q4 releases.

For RWA management, total $482 billion down 4.2% quarter-over-quarter, YTD -7.8%, CET1 13.2%, density 42%. Credit RWAs $299 billion -5.1%, sales $12 billion CRE, RMBS $15 billion. Market flat, op up modestly. Initiatives: Basel IV 85% ready, optimization $20 billion potential via reallocations, synthetics, models. Regions: NA -6%, EMEA +2%, APAC -3%. Stabilize $470-490 billion year-end.

Finally, loan outlook 4-6% FY24, C&I 5-7%, CRE 2-4%, consumer 3-8%. Regional strength Southeast. Credit: NCOs 20-30 bps, NPLs 0.70%, ACL 1.28%/177% NPLs. AI decisioning enhances.

Mark Rodriguez:
Thank you, Jennifer. From a risk management perspective, we are closely monitoring interest rate risk, credit risk, operational risk, and cyber risk. We are implementing enhanced controls and monitoring to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile.

Karen Wong:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains excellent with non-performing loans at 0.65% and allowance coverage at 1.45%. We are actively managing our loan portfolio and remain confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment.

Raj Patel:
Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our technology initiatives. We are leveraging technology to enhance customer experience, improve efficiency, and drive innovation. Our investments in AI and cloud computing are yielding significant results, from RPA and GenAI fraud models to blockchain settlements.

Laura Chen:
Good morning. We are focused on operational excellence and driving efficiency across the organization. Key initiatives include streamlining our processes, optimizing our infrastructure, and leveraging data analytics to improve decision-making.

David Kim:
Thank you. From a marketing perspective, we are focused on strengthening our brand reputation and enhancing customer engagement. Our recent marketing campaigns have been highly successful in driving customer acquisition and retention.

Susan Bailey:
Good morning. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of compliance and ethical conduct. We are continuously strengthening our compliance programs and working closely with regulators to ensure we are meeting all applicable requirements.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder to ask a question, please press star one. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson:
Good morning. Could you please provide more detail on the efficiency ratio progress and targets?

Alex Harper:
Thanks, Mike. As Jennifer outlined, we're thrilled with the 58.2% achievement and drivers like RPA and cloud migration delivering hundreds of millions in savings. Our raised FY24 guide to 57-58% and mid-50s by FY26 is achievable through GenAI and acquisitions, positioning us ahead of peers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee:
What is your outlook for loan growth and credit quality?

Jennifer Lee:
Great question, Sarah. We're guiding 4-6% growth, led by C&I and select CRE, with digital platforms accelerating originations. Credit remains pristine—NCOs 20-30 bps expected—bolstered by AI monitoring and strong coverage, even in a higher-for-longer scenario.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Brown with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Tom Brown:
Can you discuss the impact of market conditions on non-interest income?

Mark Rodriguez:
Absolutely, Tom. Markets like equity rallies and VIX elevation drove strong investment banking and trading gains, while wealth benefited from AUM growth. We're diversified to weather volatility, with Q4 outlook solid assuming constructive equity P/Es.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
What are your plans for risk-weighted assets management going forward?

Raj Patel:
Thanks, Emily. Though primarily under finance and risk, our tech backbone supports RWA optimization via advanced modeling and cloud-based simulations. We'll continue de-risking while growing low-RWA areas like sustainable finance and fees.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Alex Harper for any closing remarks.

Alex Harper:
Thank you for your interest in UniBank Financial Group. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
